title: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach
content_md: E-commerce platform Cleverbridge is warning that hackers breached its systems and stole customers' payment card information, including credit card numbers and CVV security codes. Cleverbridge provides e-commerce services to software and SaaS companies, allowing them to sell products, process payments, and manage subscriptions. The company lists numerous technology brands as its customers, including Red Hat, SUSE, Tenable, Veeam, Jamf, Sony, and Parallels. However, it has not disclosed which businesses' customers were impacted by the breach. In a new page about the security incident, Cleverbridge says it detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026, and temporarily took systems offline to contain the breach. "All systems were brought back online on 4 November 2026; however, our investigation subsequently determined that a third party copied payment card data stored on our platform," reads the security incident disclosure . Cleverbridge began notifying affected customers on November 20, warning that hackers had stolen payment card details used to make purchases through its platform. While its public disclosure confirms the theft of payment card data, it does not specify which card details were stolen, instead referring affected customers to their individual notifications for more information.
